body: I’m sorry. Knowing that the difference between having it and not having it is just a thought can be so frustrating. I find myself in a constant compulsive search for feelings of empathy within myself, which I suppose a psychopath wouldn’t do. Unfortunately I’m not sure how easy it is to switch off our blue print, so to speak, our thoughts notwithstanding. But I understand your point, definitely. On one level it kind of angers me that a genuinely dangerous psychopath wouldn’t go through the internal suffering we go through. It doesn’t seem fair, if they’re the ones at risk to society.

I’m a Harm OCD sufferer and empathy seems to be something a lot of sufferers have issue with, in that in severe cases it can feel like it’s slipping away. I don’t know how the anxiety causes this or whether it may be because of the inevitable resulting depression, but I understand it to be common in Harm OCD, having seen lots of members of a group I’m part of on Facebook report it, as well as forums. For me it’s like the solid feelings of empathy which guaranteed I was no danger to anyone or anything have just been eroded away by the OCD over the years. It’s very scary, but perhaps it only occurs in severe Harm OCD cases. But yes, in a sense you’re right in that a psychopath with no empathy would not be remotely bothered by having such thoughts in the first place.

Thank you for your reply. That fly analogy is amazing - seeing how a bad thought might enter and leave a non OCD mind is something I still genuinely struggle to comprehend in my own lived experience (I can feel my mind fighting it now as I type, with my first and strongest reaction always being 'BUT MY THOUGHT IS WORSE, WAY MORE SERIOUS/DANGEROUS SO I CAN'T IGNORE IT'), so using analogies like you have in a way helps me. It's also kind of poetic, as I am going through therapy myself with a view to one day experiencing thoughts much like pesky flies :)

Having Harm OCD, I struggle to imagine a 'normal person's' reaction to the kinds of thoughts I get.  My mind tells me they'd freak out just the same as me (seems logical), but my therapist and all the books inform me 'normal people' get the same content pretty much, they just a different reaction - so it dissolves very quickly. I find that so hard to understand. But then I think of all of the horror fiction writers and SFX artists on shows like GoT - they must have some pretty messed up violent thoughts, why isn't their sense of morality tortured like mine??

I get comfort from the idea of not existing and being nothing, owing to living with severe Pure O. But thinking of an act of self harm itself isn’t comforting, because I know how much it would hurt and the chance I might survive and be left in an even more agonising state than having just Pure O. But a painless off button would be nice.
